subject: Technical follow-up: integration architecture, SDK/auth options, and prompt governance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@finlytics.com>, Oliver Hayes <oliver@finlytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-03-09T15:12:00Z
Subject: Technical follow-up: integration architecture, SDK/auth options, and prompt governance

Hi Priya / Oliver — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what I heard you want:
- Real-time search/rerank + semantic embeddings for your analyst UX (re-rank top K for freshness).
- Structured output from the model for entity extraction and accounting-specific fields (CSV/JSON tool calling).
- Strong runtime controls for prompt versioning and injection mitigation (you called out auditability and red-team testing).

Open items we need to confirm to scope the technical deep-dive: 
1) Traffic profile: you mentioned ~150–250 qps at peak for user-search traffic, can you confirm baseline vs peak and average request size (tokens)?
2) Network posture: do you prefer outbound-only connections (private link) or can you accept VPC peering / private connectivity?
3) Auth & identity: do you have a preferred auth pattern (mTLS, OIDC, API keys + IP allowlist)?
4) SDKs & runtimes: primary languages for your services (Python/Go/Java)?
5) Embedding requirements: expected vector dim, retention policy for vectors, and whether you need incremental reindexing or full refreshes.
6) Prompt governance: who will own prompt versioning/workflow on your side (product vs. security)?

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 30–45 min technical deep-dive with Dev (solutions engineer) and Vivek (runtime infra) to walk your network/security constraints + model routing strategies — propose Wed 2026-03-11 16:00 PT.
- We'll produce a short mutual action plan and a one-pager for prompt governance (versioning, audit trail, blocking rules).
- Dev will draft SDK quickstart snippets and recommended auth patterns tailored to your environment.

If you can reply with the answers to items 1–5 and attach any network diagrams/security docs, we’ll prepare a targeted runbook for the deep-dive.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few answers inline and an attached network diagram (v2) for context. 

Answers to your questions:
1) Traffic: baseline ~60 qps, peak bursts up to ~220 qps during market opens. Average request is ~220–380 tokens (user + context).
2) Network: we cannot host inbound peering for external vendors due to our networking policy. Preferred approach is PrivateLink / outbound TLS connections.
3) Auth: long-term we prefer mTLS for internal services, but for external vendor integration we typically use short-lived OIDC tokens or API keys rotated by Vault.
4) SDKs: primary infra is Go for backend services and TypeScript for the frontend.
5) Embeddings: aiming for 1536 dim vectors, retention ~90 days for hot dataset, colder archival in S3. We do incremental upserts; full refresh quarterly.

Security asks:
- We will share our security questionnaire next week — SOC2 is mandatory.
- Need to understand how you support prompt versioning and the ability to pin prompt templates to a stable model/variant for audits.
- We’ll want a red-team plan for prompt injection and an ability to block or sanitize tool calls at runtime.

Attached: network_diagram_v2.pdf

Oliver
CTO, FinLytics
oliver@finlytics.com

Subject: Re: Technical follow-up: integration architecture, SDK/auth options, and prompt governance

Marissa / team — high level technical plan and attachments (quickstart + governance draft) below. This is an executive-technical summary; we can expand each section in the deep-dive.

1) SDK quickstart (attached sdk_quickstart.md) — highlights:
- Languages: Go + TypeScript examples included.
- Auth: hosted API recommended pattern = short-lived OIDC tokens exchanged by backend services + API keys with Vault rotation for server-to-server. For Private deployments we recommend mTLS with client cert rotation via KMS/HSM. Snippets show token refresh + retry/backoff.
- Connection: support outbound HTTPS to Redwood PrivateLink endpoints. We surface region-prefixed endpoints (us-west-2.redwood.api) and client-side failover.

2) Routing & fallbacks:
- Primary rule: route to lowest-latency compatible model variant meeting quality threshold.
- Fallbacks: use quantized medium-latency model variant when GPU contention detected; provide automatic prefix caching for repeated queries to reduce tail latency.
- Circuit breaker: if 5xx rate > 2% for 2m window, downgrade to cheaper model variant and alert.

3) Structured output / tool-calling:
- Schema-first: define a JSON Schema for your accounting extraction output (fields + types).
- Runtime: strict validator rejects non-conforming outputs; when in ambiguous cases return a well-formed "error" object instead of free text.
- Tool calls: whitelist allowed tool names + parameter schemas; all tool-call args pass canonicalization and length checks.
- Example: provided JSONSchema for "transaction_record" with required fields: txn_id, amount_cents, currency, merchant_normalized, timestamp_iso.

4) Embeddings & reranker:
- Use 1536-d vectors (matches your ask).
- Batch upserts (1k–5k vectors per request) and async ingestion; set hot TTL = 90d and cold archive to S3 every 30d/quarterly snapshot.
- Rerank pipeline: bi-encoder for candidate retrieval (index returns top 200), cross-encoder (or cross-attention reranker) for top-20 exact ranking.

5) Prompt governance (attached prompt_governance_v1.pdf) — summary:
- Storage & versioning: store canonical prompt templates in Git repo with semantic-like tags (v1.2.0-prompt) and immutable content-addressed hashes (SHA256) in metadata.
- Runtime provenance: each generation includes prompt_version, prompt_hash, author, timestamp in the generation metadata and stored in audit logs for 180 days (or longer per contract).
- Prompt-lint / static checks: run CI that enforces no inline user substitution without explicit sanitizer; detect suspicious tokens (e.g., injection patterns) and fail pipeline until reviewed.
- Injection mitigations: canonicalize user input, enforce strict separators, limit system prompt length, escape/unescape user-provided markup, and use a sanitizer that strips sequences likely to alter model instruction semantics.
- Tool-call safety: require tool schemas and an allowlist; sandbox tool execution and enforce a runtime capability check (deny if schema mismatch).
- Red-team plan: maintain an adversarial prompt corpus per vertical, run fuzzing + adversarial tests nightly against staging; fail quality gates if hallucination or schema-violation rate exceeds thresholds. Integrate tests into CI so prompt/template merges require green checks.

6) Ops & monitoring:
- Instrument token-level cost, per-prompt_version latency & error tracking, and regression alerts tied to evals.
- Offer canary rollouts for prompt template changes (10% traffic) and automatic rollback if eval fails.

Attachments: sdk_quickstart.md (one-pager), prompt_governance_v1.pdf (draft runbook).

Availability: Wed 2026-03-11 16:00 PT works for a 45-min technical deep-dive — happy to demo the SDK snippets and governance dashboard.
